Reference prototype reviewed: the supplied Netlify Enterprise Governance MVP. It contains portfolio overview, resource capacity, resource bottlenecks, risk overview, department workload, project health, executive attention items, project registry, filters, milestones, checkpoints, dependencies and change-request governance.

Validation note: the supplied Claude public artifact URL was not accessible to the document-generation environment, so this BRD uses the user-provided description plus the accessible Netlify prototype as the validated baseline. The Claude artifact should be re-reviewed during solution design before final UI sign-off.

## Executive Product Thesis

Build a single management system that connects Strategy → Investment → Portfolio → Project → MVP → Roadmap → Resource → WBS → Risk → Governance → Outcome. The platform should not merely report whether projects are on track; it should help executives decide what to START, CONTINUE, ACCELERATE, DELAY or STOP.

# 1. Executive Summary

The company needs one integrated view of its entire project portfolio. Today, portfolio information is commonly fragmented across project plans, spreadsheets, finance reports, resource plans, weekly status reports and delivery tools. This creates three management problems: lack of transparency, poor cross-project trade-off decisions, and slow escalation.

The proposed Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance Platform combines the strongest elements of the existing governance prototype with a strategic portfolio and investment layer. The existing prototype is retained as the governance and delivery foundation; strategic alignment, investment management, benefits realization, prioritization, scenario planning and AI decision support are added above it.

## Business Outcomes

- Create a single source of truth for all company projects and initiatives.

- Give executives a portfolio-level view of investment, value, resources, delivery health, risks and dependencies.

- Improve resource allocation and identify bottlenecks before they become delivery failures.

- Strengthen change control by protecting committed scope, timeline and dependency baselines.

- Connect every project to strategic objectives and measurable outcomes.

- Enable portfolio decisions to fund, accelerate, maintain, defer or stop initiatives.

- Reduce manual preparation of weekly and SteerCo portfolio reporting.

- Create a data foundation for scenario planning and an AI portfolio copilot.

# 2. Product Vision & Positioning

## 2.1 Product Vision

One enterprise platform where leadership can see what the company is investing in, why it matters, whether the company has capacity to deliver it, what is at risk, and what action should be taken.

## 2.2 Product Positioning

| **Traditional PM Tool** | **Existing Governance Prototype** | **Recommended Platform** |
|----|----|----|
| How are tasks progressing? | How are projects governed? | Are we investing in the right things and delivering the right outcomes? |
| Task / sprint focus | Project / milestone focus | Strategy / investment / portfolio / delivery / outcome |
| Mostly project-level | Portfolio visibility + governance | Enterprise strategic portfolio intelligence |
| Status reporting | Exception reporting | Decision support + scenario planning |

## 2.3 Core Management Questions

1.  What are we investing in?

2.  Why are we investing in it?

3.  How much are we investing?

4.  Do we have enough people and capability?

5.  When will the value be delivered?

6.  What is at risk or dependent on something else?

7.  Which commitments have changed?

8.  Which projects should be funded, accelerated, delayed or stopped?

# 3. Product Principles

- CEO-first, not task-first: executive views surface decisions and exceptions before detailed project data.

- One golden thread: every project should trace from strategy to investment, MVP, delivery and outcome.

- Exception-based management: highlight what needs attention instead of forcing leaders to inspect every project.

- Baseline integrity: committed scope, date, budget and dependencies require governed change.

- Single data model: project, resource, budget, roadmap, risk and outcome information should not be maintained in disconnected spreadsheets.

- Drill-down by design: executives can remain at portfolio level while delivery teams can drill to milestone, WBS and task.

- Integrate rather than replace execution tools: Jira, Azure DevOps, ERP, HR and finance remain systems of record where appropriate.

- Decision-oriented analytics: dashboards must lead to actions, not just visualization.

- AI should explain, predict and recommend using traceable portfolio data.

# 4. Scope

## 4.1 In Scope

| **Domain** | **Scope** |
|----|----|
| Strategy | Strategic pillars, objectives, KPI linkage |
| Portfolio | Portfolio hierarchy, investment allocation, prioritization |
| Project | Project master record, owner, sponsor, business case, budget, timeline |
| MVP / Product | MVP definition, features, release milestones, expected value |
| Roadmap | 12-24 month portfolio, project and MVP roadmap |
| Resource | Capacity, demand, utilization, capability bottlenecks |
| Delivery | Milestones, checkpoints, WBS, dependencies |
| Risk | Risk register, risk engine, portfolio risk aggregation |
| Governance | Weekly reports, baseline, approvals, decisions, change requests |
| Investment | Budget, actual, forecast, variance, CapEx/OpEx, value |
| Outcome | KPI, expected benefit, realized benefit, value at risk |
| AI | Portfolio Q&A, alerts, recommendations and scenario support - Phase 2/3 |

## 4.2 Out of Scope for MVP

- Full replacement of Jira/Azure DevOps or enterprise task management.

- Full accounting/ERP functionality.

- Detailed payroll or HR administration.

- Complex procurement lifecycle.

- Advanced AI autonomous actions without human approval.

## 6.1 Golden Thread

Every investment should have a traceable relationship: Strategic Objective → Portfolio → Project → MVP → Investment → Resource → Delivery → KPI / Benefit.

## 6.2 Decision Lifecycle

| **Decision** | **Trigger** | **Required Evidence** | **Outcome** |
|----|----|----|----|
| START | New initiative proposed | Business case, strategic fit, capacity, value | Approved / rejected |
| CONTINUE | Periodic review | Health, value, risk, spend | Continue / remediate |
| ACCELERATE | High value / critical opportunity | Capacity, dependency, scenario impact | Additional funding/resources |
| DELAY | Capacity or priority conflict | Strategic score, dependencies, scenario | Replanned roadmap |
| STOP | Low value / poor feasibility | Value at risk, spend, score, alternatives | Close / reallocate |

# 9. Conceptual Data Model

| **Entity** | **Key Attributes** | **Relationships** |
|----|----|----|
| Strategy | Pillar, objective, KPI, target | 1 Strategy → many objectives |
| Portfolio | Name, owner, budget, priority | Portfolio contains programs/projects |
| Program/Product | Name, owner, roadmap | Contains projects/MVPs |
| Project | ID, business case, owner, sponsor, budget, dates, status | Belongs to portfolio; contains MVPs/milestones |
| MVP | Objective, scope, KPI, release | Belongs to project/product; contains features |
| Milestone | Baseline date, forecast, status, dependencies | Belongs to project/MVP |
| WBS | Work package, owner, effort, status | Belongs to milestone/project |
| Resource | Person/capability, capacity, cost | Allocated to projects/MVPs |
| Risk | Probability, impact, owner, mitigation | Linked to project/MVP/milestone |
| Dependency | Source, target, type, date | Cross-project or internal |
| Budget | Approved, actual, forecast, variance | Linked to project/portfolio |
| Benefit | Expected, realized, owner, measurement | Linked to objective/project/MVP |
| Change Request | Baseline change, impact, approver, decision | Linked to project/milestone |
| Decision | Decision type, rationale, approver, date | Linked to portfolio/project/CR |
| Weekly Report | Period, health, narrative, changes | Linked to project |

# 10. Business Rules

| **Rule** | **Business Rule** |
|----|----|
| BR-01 | Every committed project must have an owner and sponsor. |
| BR-02 | Every committed project must have a strategic objective or an approved exemption. |
| BR-03 | Every committed project must have a baseline budget and target date. |
| BR-04 | Baseline scope, dates, budget and critical dependencies are locked after commitment. |
| BR-05 | Changes to locked fields require an approved Change Request. |
| BR-06 | Every MVP must have a measurable outcome/KPI and release criteria. |
| BR-07 | Resource utilization thresholds are configurable by capability and organization. |
| BR-08 | A project cannot be marked green if critical risk rules force a yellow/red state without an explicit override and rationale. |
| BR-09 | Missing weekly reports create an exception item. |
| BR-10 | Portfolio recommendations are advisory until an authorized executive approves the decision. |
| BR-11 | Scenario analysis must not alter approved baseline data. |
| BR-12 | All approvals and governance decisions must be auditable. |

# 11. Product & Portfolio KPIs

| **KPI** | **Definition** | **Target Direction** |
|----|----|----|
| Portfolio health | Weighted health across strategic, financial, delivery, resource and risk dimensions | ↑ |
| Strategic alignment coverage | % committed projects linked to approved objectives | 100% |
| Budget variance | Forecast vs approved budget | ↓ |
| Schedule variance | Forecast milestone completion vs baseline | ↓ |
| Capacity utilization | Demand / available capacity | Within threshold |
| Critical resource bottlenecks | \# capabilities above critical threshold | ↓ |
| Critical portfolio risks | \# critical risks | ↓ |
| Green-but-risky rate | Projects with PM green but risk engine yellow/red | ↓ |
| Change request cycle time | Median time from submission to decision | ↓ |
| Benefit realization | Realized benefit / expected benefit | ↑ |
| Decision lead time | Time from portfolio exception to executive decision | ↓ |
| Reporting compliance | Projects submitting weekly report on time | ↑ |

# 12. Roles & Permissions

| **Role** | **Create/Edit** | **Approve** | **View** |
|----|----|----|----|
| CEO / ExCo | Decisions, strategic priorities | Portfolio decisions, major CRs | All enterprise data |
| Portfolio Director / PMO | Portfolio/project governance | Portfolio-level CRs within authority | All portfolio data |
| Product Director | Projects, MVPs, roadmaps | Product/project decisions | Assigned + portfolio summary |
| Project Manager | Project, milestones, WBS, risks, weekly report | Operational changes within delegated authority | Assigned projects |
| Finance | Investment actuals/forecast | Financial controls | Portfolio investment |
| Resource Manager | Capacity/allocations | Resource changes | Resource views |
| Business Owner | Business case/KPI/benefit | Business acceptance | Owned initiatives |
| Viewer | No edit | No | Approved read-only views |

# 14. Non-Functional Requirements

| **Area** | **Requirement** |
|----|----|
| Security | SSO, RBAC, least privilege, encryption in transit/at rest, audit logs. |
| Performance | Executive dashboard should load within agreed enterprise SLA under normal portfolio volume. |
| Availability | Target enterprise availability aligned to company criticality tier. |
| Auditability | All baseline changes, approvals and decisions timestamped with actor and rationale. |
| Scalability | Support growth from hundreds to thousands of projects and users. |
| Usability | CEO can reach portfolio health and decisions within 30 seconds from home. |
| Accessibility | Follow corporate accessibility standards and keyboard-friendly interaction. |
| Data quality | Mandatory fields, validation, stale-data alerts and reconciliation controls. |
| Observability | Integration failures and stale feeds visible to administrators. |
| AI safety | AI recommendations require evidence, confidence/assumptions and human approval for action. |

# 15. Recommended Product Roadmap

| **Phase** | **Scope** | **Outcome** |
|----|----|----|
| MVP / Phase 1 | Portfolio cockpit, registry, project detail, budget, resources, timeline, MVP, roadmap, milestones, WBS, risks, dependencies, weekly reporting, CR | Single source of truth + governance |
| V2 | Strategy, benefits, investment analytics, scoring, prioritization, capacity optimization, scenario planning, SteerCo reporting | Portfolio intelligence + investment decisions |

## 15.1 MVP Success Criteria

- 100% of in-scope projects have a master record.

- 100% of committed projects have owner, sponsor, budget, timeline and status.

- Portfolio dashboard reconciles with approved project data.

- Resource bottlenecks can be identified by project and capability.

- Every baseline change is traceable to a Change Request.

- Executives can generate a weekly/SteerCo portfolio review without manual spreadsheet consolidation.

- Roadmap can show projects, MVPs and key dependencies.

- At least one pilot portfolio uses the platform as the primary governance source.

# 16. Key User Journeys

## 16.1 CEO Weekly Review

9.  Open Executive Portfolio Cockpit.

10. Review portfolio health, investment, value and capacity.

11. Open Requires Attention.

12. Review green-but-risky and material budget/resource exceptions.

13. Review recommended decisions.

14. Approve / reject / request further analysis.

15. Publish decisions into Decision Log.

## 16.2 Product Director Portfolio Review

16. Filter portfolio by strategic objective/product.

17. Review roadmap and MVP delivery.

18. Identify capacity conflicts and dependencies.

19. Review project score and expected value.

20. Create scenario if trade-offs are required.

21. Submit recommendation to governance.

## 16.3 Project Manager Weekly Update

22. Open assigned project.

23. Update progress, milestones, risks, dependencies and narrative.

24. Confirm budget and forecast.

25. Submit weekly report.

26. If a baseline changes, create Change Request rather than editing locked commitment.

# 17. Governance Model

| **Cadence** | **Forum** | **Purpose** | **Platform Output** |
|----|----|----|----|
| Weekly | Portfolio Ops | Exceptions, risks, capacity, missing reports | Attention queue + actions |
| Bi-weekly | Product / Program Review | Roadmap, MVP, dependencies, resources | Updated roadmap + decisions |
| Monthly | Portfolio Review | Investment, health, benefits, strategic alignment | Portfolio scorecard |
| Quarterly | SteerCo / ExCo | Investment allocation and strategic trade-offs | Decision pack + scenario options |
| Ad hoc | Change Control | Material scope/budget/date/dependency changes | CR decision + audit trail |

# 18. UX / Wireframe Principles

- Use progressive disclosure: summary first, detail on demand.

- Keep executive screens decision-oriented.

- Use consistent RAG semantics but do not rely on color alone.

- Every warning should have a reason and next action.

- Every portfolio metric should be drillable to underlying projects.

- Use baseline vs forecast vs actual consistently.

- Keep strategic, investment and execution information visually connected.

- Show confidence / data freshness for calculated indicators.

- Avoid dashboard overload: prioritize 5-8 high-value executive signals.

## Final Recommendation

- Position the product as Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance, not merely project management.

- Preserve the prototype's strongest features: control tower, exceptions, capacity, risk, project health and change governance.

- Add the missing executive layer: strategy, investment, benefits, prioritization and scenario planning.

- Use Strategy → Investment → Project → MVP → Delivery → Outcome as the core data model.

- Make Executive Attention and Decision Center the first-class experience.

- Use integrations to avoid forcing teams to duplicate Jira, ERP or HR data.

- Build AI only after the portfolio data model and governance rules are trusted.

- Pilot with one portfolio, prove decision value, then scale enterprise-wide.

# BRD v3.0 - Workspace & Governance Framework Layer

Product Director Change: add a configurable Workspace layer above Portfolio / Project management. Each company, business unit or governed operating environment can operate inside its own Workspace with a reusable delivery-and-governance framework template. Templates can be cloned, adapted, reviewed and published for another workspace without changing the common enterprise data model.

## 1. Product Concept: Workspace

A Workspace is the configurable operating container in which a company or organizational unit manages its portfolio, projects, governance and delivery lifecycle. It separates company-specific operating rules from the platform's common data model.

| **Concept** | **Definition** | **Example** |
|----|----|----|
| Platform | Shared enterprise product and common data model | Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence Platform |
| Workspace | Governed environment for a company, BU, program or operating model | Company A - Workspace A |
| Workspace Template | Reusable blueprint of lifecycle and governance configuration | Digital Product Delivery v1 |
| Project Template | Reusable project structure instantiated inside a workspace | Discovery → Design → Solution → Development → Test → GTM → Retro |
| Project Instance | Actual project created from a template | Company A - Mobile App Transformation |

## 2. Updated Target Hierarchy

PLATFORM → WORKSPACE → PORTFOLIO → PROGRAM / PRODUCT → PROJECT → MVP → FEATURE → MILESTONE / WBS

Cross-cutting layers remain Strategy, Investment, Resources, Risks, Dependencies, Governance and Outcomes.

- Workspace is a governance boundary: configuration, roles, templates, approval policies and reporting scope can differ by workspace.

- The same core data model is reused across workspaces to preserve enterprise consistency.

- A project belongs to one active workspace at a time; controlled cross-workspace dependencies can be supported.

- Workspace configuration must never silently alter historical project records or approved baselines.

## 3. Workspace Management - Business Requirements

| **ID** | **Priority** | **Requirement** | **Acceptance Criteria** |
|----|----|----|----|
| WS-001 | P0 | Create Workspace | Authorized admin creates workspace with name, company/BU, owner, timezone, fiscal calendar and status. |
| WS-002 | P0 | Workspace isolation | Users see only authorized workspaces and records. |
| WS-003 | P0 | Workspace profile | Store purpose, operating model, governance owner, currency, calendar and reporting cadence. |
| WS-004 | P0 | Workspace switcher | Users can switch between authorized workspaces without losing context. |
| WS-005 | P0 | Workspace dashboard | Show portfolio health, investment, capacity, risk, governance exceptions and upcoming gates. |
| WS-006 | P0 | Workspace lifecycle | Draft, Active, Suspended and Archived states; archived workspace is read-only/auditable. |
| WS-007 | P1 | Workspace cloning | Clone workspace configuration into a new workspace without live transactions unless explicitly selected. |
| WS-008 | P1 | Cross-workspace governance | Support controlled shared resources, dependencies and executive reporting. |
| WS-009 | P0 | Auditability | Record actor, timestamp, before/after value and reason for configuration changes. |
| WS-010 | P0 | Configuration versioning | Published framework versions are immutable; changes create a new version. |

## 4. Governance / Delivery Framework Template

The Workspace Framework Template defines how work moves from idea to outcome. It is configurable rather than hard-coded.

Reference - Company A: DISCOVERY → DESIGN → SOLUTION → DEVELOPMENT → TEST → GTM → RETRO / CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

- Each stage has purpose, activities, owner, entry criteria, mandatory artifacts, gate, exit criteria, SLA and dependencies.

- Stages may be sequential, optional, conditional or parallel.

- Gate rules can require Product, Business, Technology, Risk, Finance, Legal, Security or other configured approvals.

- A framework can be cloned and adapted for another workspace.

- Published versions are immutable; projects retain the framework version with which they were instantiated.

## 5. Stage & Gate - Business Requirements

| **ID** | **Priority** | **Requirement** | **Acceptance Criteria** |
|----|----|----|----|
| GF-001 | P0 | Stage library | Admin can create, edit, deactivate and reorder lifecycle stages. |
| GF-002 | P0 | Stage metadata | Objective, description, owner, duration/SLA, activities, artifacts, entry and exit criteria supported. |
| GF-003 | P0 | Gate configuration | Approvers, quorum, decision options and evidence requirements configurable per gate. |
| GF-004 | P0 | Mandatory artifacts | Documents, fields, checklists and evidence can be mandatory before gate submission. |
| GF-005 | P0 | Role mapping | Stages map to configurable workspace roles. |
| GF-006 | P0 | Conditional flow | Rules can add/remove stages, e.g. regulatory impact = yes → Compliance Review. |
| GF-007 | P1 | Parallel stages | Selected activities can run in parallel with dependency controls. |
| GF-008 | P0 | Gate decision | Pass, Pass with Conditions, Rework, Hold and Reject with rationale/evidence. |
| GF-009 | P0 | Exit criteria | Project cannot advance until mandatory criteria pass or an authorized waiver exists. |
| GF-010 | P1 | Stage SLA | Track planned vs actual duration and overdue stages. |
| GF-011 | P1 | Stage health | Combine schedule, scope, resources, risks, dependencies and gate readiness. |
| GF-012 | P1 | Framework versioning | Project stage instances retain their source framework version. |
| GF-013 | P1 | Framework analytics | Aggregate stage distribution, bottlenecks, gate failures and cycle time. |
| GF-014 | P0 | Exception / waiver | Authorized users can temporarily waive a rule with reason, approver and expiry. |

## 6. Company A Reference Framework

| **Stage** | **Purpose** | **Typical Mandatory Outputs** | **Gate / Exit** |
|----|----|----|----|
| Discovery | Validate problem, customer need, opportunity and strategic fit | Problem statement, customer evidence, opportunity, initial business case, KPI | Discovery approval |
| Design | Define experience, process and target operating model | Journey/service blueprint, UX/UI, process design, acceptance criteria | Design approval |
| Solution | Define technical/business solution and feasibility | Architecture, NFRs, integrations, security/risk assessment, estimate | Solution approval |
| Development | Build approved scope | Sprint/release plan, WBS, code/review evidence, progress, dependencies | Build readiness |
| Test | Validate quality, security, performance and business acceptance | Test evidence, defects, UAT, security/performance results | Go-live readiness |
| GTM | Prepare launch, adoption and operational readiness | Launch plan, training, communication, support model, KPI baseline | GTM / launch approval |
| Retro / Improvement | Measure outcome and improve delivery system | Outcome review, KPI result, lessons learned, improvement actions | Closure / improvement backlog |

## 7. Template Clone & Adaptation

The template model should behave as a governed configuration system: CLONE → ADAPT → REVIEW → PUBLISH → INSTANTIATE.

| **ID** | **Priority** | **Requirement** | **Acceptance Criteria** |
|----|----|----|----|
| TPL-001 | P0 | Template catalog | Authorized users browse approved corporate and workspace templates. |
| TPL-002 | P0 | Clone template | Existing template can be cloned into an editable draft. |
| TPL-003 | P0 | Adapt stages | Add, remove, rename, reorder and configure stages. |
| TPL-004 | P0 | Adapt governance | Change approvers, artifacts, gates, thresholds and exception rules. |
| TPL-005 | P0 | Publish workflow | Changes require review and publication before activation. |
| TPL-006 | P0 | Template version | Each published version has unique version and effective date. |
| TPL-007 | P0 | Template provenance | Record source template, lineage, author and changes. |
| TPL-008 | P1 | Template comparison | Compare versions and show stage/rule/artifact differences. |
| TPL-009 | P1 | Template migration | Propose migration of active projects and show impact before approval. |
| TPL-010 | P1 | Template library | Support global standard templates plus workspace-specific templates. |

## 8. Governance Gate Operating Model

Governance should be embedded into the lifecycle, not represented only as a reporting layer.

PROPOSE → DISCOVER → GATE → DESIGN → GATE → SOLUTION → GATE → BUILD → TEST GATE → GTM GATE → OUTCOME / RETRO

- Gate readiness is visible before meetings: required evidence, open risks, dependencies, budget/resource impact and decision history.

- Approvers can request information or rework without bypassing baseline/change-control rules.

- Gate decisions are linked to project, stage, evidence, approver and Decision Log.

- Failed/conditional gates can create actions, risks or change requests automatically.

- Escalation rules trigger for overdue, repeatedly failed or materially blocked gates.

## 9. Workspace Roles

| Platform Admin | Owns global platform configuration and standard template library. |
| Workspace Owner | Owns workspace purpose, governance model, users and framework configuration. |
| Portfolio Manager | Controls portfolio health, prioritization, investment and cross-project trade-offs. |
| Project Owner / PM | Executes lifecycle and maintains stage evidence. |
| Stage Owner | Owns readiness and delivery of a specific stage. |
| Gate Approver | Makes formal gate decision within delegated authority. |
| Business Owner / Sponsor | Owns business case, strategic alignment and outcomes. |
| Control Function | Risk, Finance, Security, Legal or Compliance review where configured. |
| Executive / ExCo | Makes portfolio-level investment and exception decisions. |

## 12. New Data Model

| **Entity** | **Key Attributes** | **Relationships** |
|----|----|----|
| Workspace | ID, name, company/BU, owner, status, config, version | Contains portfolios/projects; owns framework versions |
| Workspace Framework | ID, workspace, version, status, effective date | Contains stages, gates, rules and templates |
| Lifecycle Stage | ID, name, sequence, type, SLA, criteria | Belongs to framework; instantiated by project |
| Gate | ID, decision type, approvers, quorum, criteria | Belongs to stage; records decisions |
| Stage Artifact | Type, mandatory flag, owner, status, evidence | Required by stage/gate |
| Stage Rule | Condition, action, threshold | Controls routing/escalation |
| Framework Version | Version, parent, change summary, publisher | Projects reference version used |
| Project Stage Instance | Project, stage, dates, status, readiness | Instantiates framework stage |
| Gate Decision | Decision, rationale, approver, timestamp, evidence | Linked to gate/project |
| Exception / Waiver | Rule, reason, approver, expiry | Temporarily overrides governance rule |

## 13. New Business Rules

- A project cannot be created without a workspace.

- Every active workspace has one published default framework.

- A project instantiated from a framework stores the exact framework version used.

- Editing a template does not retroactively alter existing project stage instances.

- A governed stage cannot be Complete if mandatory exit criteria are incomplete unless an approved waiver exists.

- Gate decisions are immutable after approval except through a correction workflow.

- Committed scope, budget, target date and critical dependencies remain subject to the existing Change Request process.

- Workspace configuration changes require role-based authorization and audit logging.

- Cross-workspace reporting respects record-level permissions.

- Archived workspace configurations and historical gate decisions remain auditable.

## 15. New Workspace Governance KPIs

- Stage cycle time: planned vs actual duration

- Gate pass / conditional pass / rework rate

- First-pass gate approval rate

- Time waiting for governance decision

- Stage bottleneck volume and aging

- Mandatory evidence completion rate

- Exception / waiver rate and overdue waiver rate

- Framework compliance rate by workspace

- Rework caused by failed gates

- Framework-version impact on delivery cycle time, quality and outcomes

- Cross-workspace benchmarks where policy permits

## 17. Updated Product Vision

The platform becomes a configurable Enterprise Portfolio Operating System: a common portfolio data and decision layer combined with workspace-specific operating frameworks.

ONE PLATFORM → MANY WORKSPACES → CONFIGURABLE GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORKS → STANDARDIZED DATA → LOCAL OPERATING MODELS → PORTFOLIO INTELLIGENCE

The strategic principle is: standardize the data and decision language; configure the operating workflow.

## 18. Product Director Recommendation

- Make Workspace a first-class product object, not a folder or filter.

- Keep the core portfolio data model standardized across all workspaces.

- Make governance lifecycle configurable through templates rather than custom development.

- Separate Template Definition from Project Execution so template changes never silently rewrite live project history.

- Treat versioning, gate evidence, exceptions and audit trail as foundational capabilities.

- Design the standard configuration workflow as Clone → Adapt → Review → Publish → Instantiate.

- Expand M08 Governance & Change into a Lifecycle Governance Engine.

- Measure framework performance so the organization can continuously improve how projects are delivered.
